outcome: Detections are triaged and acted on around the clock, without the business having to staff and run its own security team.
overview: A mid-sized business cannot staff a security operations centre and should not pretend otherwise: detections arrive at three in the morning whether or not anyone is there. Falcon Complete is a managed service where the vendor’s own analysts triage and respond on the customer’s behalf, within a scope agreed in advance. The clause that decides whether this works is that scope: what the service may do without asking, what it must ask about, and how it reaches someone at three in the morning when it does.

benefits.text: Detections are triaged and responded to around the clock without the customer staffing it
benefits.limits: The service acts within a contracted scope; anything outside it waits for a customer decision, which is where the escalation path matters

benefits.text: Response actions are taken by analysts who work on this platform continuously
benefits.limits: The service knows the platform, not the customer’s business; deciding whether a machine may be isolated during a working shift still needs customer context

benefits.text: Security outcomes stop depending on hiring in a market where the skills are scarce
benefits.limits: The platform is agent-and-cloud, so telemetry leaves the customer estate; the tenant region is a design decision to be made and recorded rather than a default to be accepted

residency: Telemetry is processed in the vendor tenant in a selected region; the service’s analysts operate against that tenant

notFor.situation: An organisation with a staffed round-the-clock security operations function
notFor.why: The service duplicates a capability that exists and creates ambiguity about who acts

notFor.situation: An organisation unwilling to grant the service any authority to act
notFor.why: A service that must ask before every action provides monitoring, not response, and should be priced as such

scope:
Model: Vendor-delivered managed service with Redington holding the commercial relationship and the scope and review process · Duration: 3–5 weeks from sensor rollout to service start with escalation tested
Support model: Continuous managed detection and response by the vendor within the contracted scope; Redington coordinates the commercial relationship and the quarterly scope review.
1) Scope — action scope agreed, escalation contacts named, residency position recorded
2) Deploy — sensor rolled out across the estate
3) Test — out-of-hours escalation path exercised end to end
4) Start and hand over — service live with monthly reporting, review cadence handed over
deliverables: An out-of-hours escalation reaches a named contact within the contracted time, demonstrated by test
The action scope is documented and the service’s actions are traceable to it
Monthly reporting states the share of detections handled entirely within scope
effort: 3–5 weeks from sensor rollout to service start with escalation tested
